newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Rusplats sees no immediate end to strike.
newsitem.headline: Rusplats sees no immediate end to strike.

text.p: South Africa's Rustenburg Platinum Holdings Ltd, the world's biggest platinum producer, said on Wednesday there was no immediate end in sight to a wildcat strike which has affected 15-20 percent of production.
"We are in constant dialogue with the NUM (National Union of Mineworkers). But I don't see any solution yet," said Johan Adler, spokesman for holding company Anglo American Platinum Corp Ltd.
The strike by about 4,600 workers from two of three hostels on the Amandelbult section of the mine began on Monday night.
Adler said it was very unlikely that the afternoon shift, due to start at 2.00 p.m. (1200 GMT), from the affected hostels would go down the mine.
The problem started when employees at two Amandelbult workers hostels took illegal industrial action over the Friday sacking of an employee.
The workers did not turn up for Monday's night shift and a fight broke out at one of the hostels between strikers and employees who wanted to work. One worker was injured.
The NUM is opposed to the illegal strike which analysts say reflects a long-running dispute over union representation.

Prices of the platinum group metals (PGMs) surged to fresh highs on Wednesday on news of the unofficial strike. Platinum fixed in London at $404.50 an ounce, its highest since August 1, 1996 and up from $398.00 previously.
